reachability.summary: Reachable through validator CLI/validate API when used on another party's submission. Fixed bundled model-only integration does not require this path.

attackPath.summary: An attacker supplies a bot for validation; operator invokes the optional validator; module import executes the attacker's top-level code with validator privileges.

codeEvidence.explanation: After a submission passes the denylist, its resolved path is forwarded to the host importer.
codeEvidence.label: Validation imports submitted source after static checks

codeEvidence.explanation: Calls via names imported from permitted os are not in the banned builtin list; os is explicitly allowed at lines 42-56.
codeEvidence.label: Only selected direct call names are blocked

codeEvidence.code:
def load_bot(path: str):
    spec   = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("bot_under_test", path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
codeEvidence.explanation: exec_module evaluates arbitrary top-level submission Python without an isolation boundary.
codeEvidence.label: Submission module executes in validator process

confidence.rationale: Independent source review confirms both bypassable checks and unsandboxed exec_module; no exploit was executed.

originalCandidates.control: bot submission author controls bot.py passed to validate/CLI
originalCandidates.counterevidence: Requires operator passing attacker-controlled submission; tests/test_smoke.py uses fixed repository bot. Docker controls in match.py do not cover validator. No public remote submission endpoint identified.
originalCandidates.evidence: check_static lines221-227 allows from os import system because os is permitted; lines258-280 only reject selected Name calls and attributes spelled os.*. A top-level system(...) via imported alias passes these checks. validate lines523-534 then load_bot exec_module line347 executes it directly in host process, before any Docker sandbox. CLI570 and Makefile19 reach this path.
originalCandidates.impact: An operator validating an untrusted bot grants host-user code execution, files/environment/network access; this is a validator vulnerability, not evidence shipped bot is malware.
originalCandidates.remediation: Do not treat AST blacklist as security boundary; run import and decide validation only inside independently killed isolated worker/container without host secrets or writable host mounts; keep static checks as lint only.

findings.remediation: Run all import-time and decision-time validation in a separate restricted process/container without host credentials or writable host mounts. Treat AST checks as lint, not isolation.

rootCause.summary: The CLI accepts an external bot path. check_static allows os imports and matches only specific names or literal os attributes, so an imported system alias is not rejected. validate then calls load_bot, whose exec_module executes submission code inside the host validator.

severity.rationale: Host code execution has high impact, but requires an operator to run the optional local validator on an attacker-supplied submission; no remote submission endpoint is present.

findings.summary: 可選的比賽驗證器以可繞過的 AST 黑名單檢查外來 bot.py，隨後直接在驗證程序匯入它。惡意提交者可藉由未被識別的匯入別名取得驗證主機使用者的程式執行權限；這不是固定主模型含有惡意程式的證據。
findings.title: 驗證外來 Bot 可在主機直接執行其程式

validation.summary: Source trace confirms a submission using a from-os import can pass the denylist and execute at module import. Docker controls exist only in the separate match launcher, not this validator. No target code or payload was executed.

dataflow.summary: bot_paths -> BotProcess -> runner.load_bot -> import-time nontermination -> parent warmup stdout.readline.

reachability.summary: Optional run_match/CLI accept bot paths; default local mode and Docker mode both share the unbounded parent wait. Fixed main model has no observed malicious trigger.

attackPath.summary: Operator includes an attacker-supplied bot in a match. Its import does not return or emit a response; the parent remains blocked waiting for warmup.

codeEvidence.explanation: If the child remains alive but produces no newline, the parent cannot advance or reach cleanup.
codeEvidence.label: Parent warmup waits without a deadline

codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker-controlled module import happens before the timeout call at line 103, outside its enforcement.
codeEvidence.label: Child imports bot before timed decisions

confidence.rationale: The parent readline has no deadline and child module import precedes the timeout; source path independently confirmed.

originalCandidates.control: untrusted submitted bot controls import-time behavior and stdout/stderr in runner
originalCandidates.counterevidence: Ordinary decide exceptions/timeouts are handled by runner103-123. Fixed trusted runtime does not expose arbitrary submission author capability; no claim of container escape.
originalCandidates.evidence: Parent warmup/read and act use blocking readline without deadline (187,161). runner main76 imports bot before timed _call_with_timeout103; top-level loop/sleep never reaches warmup timeout. run_match239-240 invokes warmup before try/finally242, so cleanup is not reached. Docker CPU/memory limits121-129 do not impose wall-clock deadline.
originalCandidates.impact: A submitted bot can hang a match indefinitely even with USE_DOCKER=true; CLI360 and demo.py286/341 have no outer timeout. Unconsumed stderr PIPE also permits backpressure; primary finding is import/warmup boundary.
originalCandidates.remediation: Enforce host-side startup and per-response wall-clock deadlines; bounded framed output and drained capped stderr; kill/reap container using owned ID, and include startup/warmup inside cleanup finally.

findings.remediation: Enforce host-side startup and per-response deadlines, bounded output and drained stderr, and kill/reap the owned process or container on timeout. Cover startup and warmup with cleanup finally.

rootCause.summary: run_match warms each subprocess before its cleanup try/finally. warmup and act block on stdout.readline without an external deadline. The child imports bot source before starting the timed decision loop, so import-time nontermination never reaches the timer.

severity.rationale: Availability impact is limited to optional local tournament jobs, requires running an attacker-supplied bot, and does not establish remote exposure or container escape.

findings.summary: 可選的比賽工具在主機端無期限等待 Bot 的啟動與動作回覆。Bot 匯入發生於計時控制之前，因此惡意提交可在匯入階段卡住比賽，即使啟用 Docker 仍然如此。
findings.title: 外來 Bot 可讓比賽程序無限等待

validation.summary: Reviewed parent and child control flow: no deadline surrounds parent I/O; Docker only constrains CPU/memory/network and does not set a runtime limit. Ordinary decide timeouts do not cover import. No hanging payload was run.
